label: Workshop 1
title: Email Multi-LoRA
summary: Train a generalist plus operations, finance and travel LoRA adapters on a small base model, compare them with a lexical baseline and learned routing (part A), then train per-persona reply adapters that later become PersonaDesk's writers (part B).
hardware: CPU is enough for the 0.5B default; a GPU is faster and recommended for part B

commands.label: Unit tests
commands.note: Training tests are skipped unless the [training] extra is installed.

commands.label: Short pipeline run: train
commands.note: Needs the [training] extra and a CUDA GPU.

prompts.label: Explain Multi-LoRA
prompts.prompt: In plain language, explain what a LoRA adapter is and why serving several adapters on one base model (Multi-LoRA) is cheaper than serving several fine-tuned models. Use the email classification workshop in workshops/email-multilora as the example.

prompts.label: Generalist vs specialists
prompts.prompt: Workshop 1 compares a generalist adapter, specialist adapters and learned routing. What trade-offs should I look for in the results, and what would make me pick one over the others?
